draft.title: Consumer credit
card: Consumer credit is money a person borrows for personal or household use, such as a car loan, a personal loan or a credit card.
The National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009 (Cth) is the main law on this. It sets rules for the businesses that lend to consumers.
lenders must hold an Australian credit licence before they can offer credit to consumers.
before giving a loan, a lender must make reasonable checks on the borrower's finances and needs. It must not give a loan that is unsuitable for the borrower.
draft.remember: Credit law works on the lender: it must be licensed and must check a loan is not unsuitable.

a.q: Which duty does the National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009 place on lenders?
opts: Hold a credit licence before offering credit to consumers
Offer the same interest rate to every borrower
Approve every loan application from a consumer
Provide credit only to people who already own property
a.why: The Act requires lenders to be licensed, so only approved businesses can lend to consumers. It does not make lenders approve every application, because a lender must refuse a loan that is unsuitable.
a.clue: The Act sets conditions on who may lend.

b.q: Dev earns a low wage. A licensed lender gives him a large loan without checking his income or expenses. Which duty has the lender most likely breached?
opts: Checking that the loan is not unsuitable for Dev
Refusing to lend to anyone on a low wage
Lending only to buyers of household goods
b.why: The lender must make reasonable checks on a borrower's finances and must not give an unsuitable loan. It was licensed, so the licence duty was met. The law does not ban lending to people on low wages, it requires the lender to check first.
b.clue: The lender was licensed, so look at what it did before lending.

a.best: Hold a credit licence before offering credit to consumers

b.best: Checking that the loan is not unsuitable for Dev
